title: Exodus, again
tomorrow: what does God want? one prophet answers in a single line.

segments.voice: Genesis asked where art thou, and the answer it waits for is here I am. Today, a whole people answers by walking out.

Most rule lists open with the rules: the lease, the team handbook, the terms nobody reads. God's commandments open with a reminder instead. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage." Before a single thou shalt, a rescue. The rules are handed to people who have just walked free.
screen: `THE TERMS NOBODY READS.` → `BEFORE THE RULES, A RESCUE.` → `OUT OF THE HOUSE OF BONDAGE.`

segments.voice: Exodus tells that walk through things you can touch. On the last night in Egypt, the people eat in a hurry, dressed to go: belts tied, sandals on, a staff in every hand. The bread has no time to rise, so it's flat. Then the sea: water on both sides, wet sand underfoot, and a crowd of former slaves walking through to the far shore. Jews still retell that night at the Passover table with the flat bread in front of them. Catholics carry it into the Easter Vigil, in the dark, by candlelight, where the crossing of the sea is the reading the Missal says is never to be left out. Paul even says the people were baptized in the cloud and in the sea, so Catholics hear water and freedom together. One more thing to tell a friend tonight. Moses never asks Pharaoh just to let the people go. The full request is to let them go so they can worship God in the desert. Freedom in Exodus has a direction: out of one house, toward a covenant and a home. Matthew even hears the whole story again in the child Jesus, called out of Egypt. That's the carry: out of Egypt, and toward something.
screen: `SANDALS ON, A STAFF IN HAND.` · `BREAD WITH NO TIME TO RISE.` · `THE SEA, AT THE EASTER VIGIL.` · `FREE FOR SOMETHING.` · then, large: `OUT OF EGYPT.`

segments.voice: Take your keys in your hand, or any key you have. Feel the teeth of it, the cold, the weight. Name one freedom you've found, silently or out loud: from a fear, a habit, a room you couldn't leave. Keep the key in your palm through the sit as the sign of it.
Exodus. The going out: Israel brought out of slavery in Egypt, through the sea, toward a freedom with a purpose.
Keep this: out of egypt, and the rules came after the rescue, not before. Day done.
